checks.label: The two sides in an equation are equal, but in an inequality one side may be greater than (or less than) the other: every inequality here holds for a whole stretch of numbers, while the equation in the explanation holds for just one

You can check the solution by substituting the value into the equation, and an inequality the same way: a right answer's numbers put back come out true inside its stretch and false outside it, and each wrong pick puts back a number that comes out the wrong way, in red

When we divide or multiply an inequality by a positive number the sign stays the same, and by a negative number the sign reverses: on the mirror screen each negative move swaps the two dots and flips the sign, each positive one keeps both, and the positive undo moves keep the order
Every puzzle accepts only the answer that matches its inequality at every number from −20 to 20 in halves (whole loads 0 to 20 on the circuit), and each wrong answer differs from it

Every line of working adds up: at x = 5 the sides make 13 and 11, then 10 and 8, then 5 and 4; at x = −5 they make −15 and −12, then −5 and −4; the moves send 10 and 15 to −10 and −15, −50 and −75, −2 and −3, or 2 and 3; every line of both routes has the same answers as 7 − 3x ≥ 1; and every number put back makes what its row says

The circle is unshaded for < and > and shaded for ≤ and ≥: every stretch is drawn to that rule, its circle on the end number, open or filled (one filled dot for =), running the way the sign points, and the circuit draws only the whole loads in each answer

Only reverse the inequality symbol when you multiply or divide each side by a negative number: on the minus-in-sight screen and the puzzle after it a minus sign is in sight, but every move is by a positive number and the sign stays
Before an answer, a puzzle shows its answers as stretches and puts no number back; a right answer then puts its numbers back on its own line
The marker tries any number: at every half from 0 to 6 it sits on its number, and the line beside it says true exactly when the number is greater than 3

Every demonstration (each move on the mirror screen too) has finished arriving within 5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends, and a pressed move plays straight away and is done within the same time; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 1.5 s
